section: Federal structure of India - features of federalism and unitary bias; Seventh Schedule (three lists), residuary powers
subsections: Switching between federal and unitary modes - emergency, Art. 249, Art. 356
Supreme Court characterisations of Indian federalism

accepted.s: Which Article enables Parliament to legislate on a subject in the State List when the Rajya Sabha declares that it is necessary in the national interest?
o: Article 356
Article 252
Article 250
Article 249
accepted.x: Article 249 empowers Parliament to legislate on a State List subject following a Rajya Sabha resolution in the national interest.
accepted.tq: Identify the Article from the specific constitutional trigger.
accepted.sec: Switching between federal and unitary modes - emergency, Art. 249, Art. 356

accepted.s: A resolution of the Rajya Sabha under Article 249 remains in force for:
o: Two years and may be renewed only once
The duration of the Lok Sabha
One year and may be renewed
Six months and cannot be renewed
accepted.x: An Article 249 resolution is valid for one year and may be renewed. It permits Parliament to legislate on a State List subject in the national interest.
accepted.tq: Separate the duration of the resolution from the duration of the law made under it.
accepted.sec: Switching between federal and unitary modes - emergency, Art. 249, Art. 356

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the effect of a National Emergency:
1. The executive power of the Union extends to giving directions to States.
2. Parliament can legislate on matters in the State List.
3. The President may modify the distribution of revenues between the Union and the States.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three are consequences of a National Emergency. The Union may direct State executive action, Parliament may legislate on State List matters, and the President may modify revenue distribution subject to parliamentary approval.
accepted.tq: Test the three dimensions of emergency centralisation: executive, legislative and financial.
accepted.sec: Switching between federal and unitary modes - emergency, Art. 249, Art. 356

accepted.s: With reference to a law made by Parliament on a State List subject during a National Emergency, which one of the following is correct?
o: It requires approval by every State Legislature to continue
It lapses six months after the emergency ends
It lapses immediately when the emergency ends
It becomes permanently applicable after the emergency ends
accepted.x: A law made by Parliament on a State List matter under Article 250 ceases to have effect six months after the National Emergency ends.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the emergency period from the six-month post-emergency validity period.
accepted.sec: Switching between federal and unitary modes - emergency, Art. 249, Art. 356

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding financial consequences of a National Emergency is NOT correct?
o: Transfers to States may be reduced or cancelled, subject to parliamentary approval.
The President may increase the transfer of funds to States as an obligatory consequence of the emergency.
The Union may issue directions affecting the financial relationship with the States.
The President may modify the distribution of revenues between the Union and the States.
accepted.x: The President may modify the distribution of revenues and may reduce or cancel transfers to States, subject to Parliament’s approval. An increase in transfers is not the specified consequence.
accepted.tq: Find the reversed financial consequence rather than accepting every emergency-related statement.
accepted.sec: Switching between federal and unitary modes - emergency, Art. 249, Art. 356

accepted.s: Article 19 is suspended during a National Emergency only when the emergency is proclaimed on the ground of:
o: Failure of constitutional machinery in a State
External emergency involving war or external aggression
Armed rebellion
Internal disturbance
accepted.x: Article 19 is automatically suspended only when the National Emergency is based on war or external aggression. Article 20 and Article 21 cannot be suspended under Article 359 orders.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the grounds of emergency for the limited suspension of Fundamental Rights.
accepted.sec: Switching between federal and unitary modes - emergency, Art. 249, Art. 356

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes a Financial Emergency under Article 360?
o: The President may dissolve every State Legislature immediately.
Parliament may legislate on every State List subject without further conditions.
The Centre may direct States to observe canons of financial propriety.
The Supreme Court may suspend the distribution of all taxes.
accepted.x: During a Financial Emergency, the Centre may direct States to observe canons of financial propriety. Other consequences include reduction of salaries and reservation of State Money Bills for the President.
accepted.tq: Ask which authority performs the specified financial function.
accepted.sec: Switching between federal and unitary modes - emergency, Art. 249, Art. 356

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: National Emergency — Article 356
President’s Rule — Article 360
Financial Emergency — Article 360
Financial Emergency — Article 249
accepted.x: Article 360 deals with Financial Emergency. Article 352 concerns National Emergency, Article 356 concerns failure of constitutional machinery in a State, and Article 249 concerns legislation on State List matters in the national interest.
accepted.tq: Use Article-number matching and reject the neighbouring constitutional provisions.
accepted.sec: Switching between federal and unitary modes - emergency, Art. 249, Art. 356

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. A proclamation of National Emergency requires parliamentary approval within one month.
2. Approval requires a special majority.
3. Once approved, the proclamation is renewable every six months.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: A National Emergency must be approved by both Houses within one month by the prescribed special majority and may continue through successive six-month approvals.
accepted.tq: Combine the approval period, majority and renewal rules in one constitutional sequence.
accepted.sec: Switching between federal and unitary modes - emergency, Art. 249, Art. 356

accepted.s: Parliamentary approval of a proclamation under Article 356 must be obtained within:
o: Six months
One month
Two months
One year
accepted.x: A proclamation of President’s Rule under Article 356 must be approved by Parliament within two months by a simple majority.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the two-month Article 356 period from the one-month National Emergency period.
accepted.sec: Switching between federal and unitary modes - emergency, Art. 249, Art. 356

accepted.s: Which of the following conditions is required for continuation of President’s Rule beyond one year?
o: Approval by all State Legislatures
A special majority in the Rajya Sabha alone
A National Emergency in operation and certification by the Election Commission
A resolution of the Inter-State Council
accepted.x: Continuation of President’s Rule beyond one year requires that a National Emergency is in operation and that the Election Commission certifies the difficulty of holding elections in the State.
accepted.tq: Identify the additional safeguards attached to extension beyond the normal period.
accepted.sec: Switching between federal and unitary modes - emergency, Art. 249, Art. 356

accepted.s:
Arrange the following National Emergencies in chronological order:
A. Emergency proclaimed in 1975
B. Emergency proclaimed in 1962
C. Emergency proclaimed in 1971
o: B, C, A
A, B, C
C, B, A
B, A, C
accepted.x: The National Emergencies mentioned were proclaimed in 1962, 1971 and 1975, respectively. Therefore, the correct order is B, C, A.
accepted.tq: Arrange the dates from earliest to latest before checking the coded options.
accepted.sec: Switching between federal and unitary modes - emergency, Art. 249, Art. 356

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about the 1975 National Emergency is correct?
o: It was proclaimed on 25 June 1975 by President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed on the ground of internal disturbance.
It was proclaimed by Parliament after the 44th Amendment on the ground of internal disturbance.
It was proclaimed on 25 June 1975 by the President on the ground of external aggression.
It was proclaimed on 26 January 1975 by the Union Cabinet on the ground of armed rebellion.
accepted.x: President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed proclaimed the Emergency on 25 June 1975 on the ground of internal disturbance.
accepted.tq: Combine the date, constitutional ground and constitutional authority in one precise recall question.
accepted.sec: Switching between federal and unitary modes - emergency, Art. 249, Art. 356

accepted.s:
With reference to safeguards introduced or strengthened by the Forty-fourth Amendment, consider the following statements:
1. The proclamation of Emergency must be based on the written advice of the Union Cabinet.
2. Notice by one-tenth of the Lok Sabha members can require a special sitting within fourteen days to consider disapproval.
3. The expression ‘internal disturbance’ was retained as a ground for Emergency.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the Forty-fourth Amendment replaced ‘internal disturbance’ with ‘armed rebellion’.
accepted.tq: Find the one statement that reverses a major safeguard introduced by the amendment.
accepted.sec: Switching between federal and unitary modes - emergency, Art. 249, Art. 356

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the constitutional significance of Part XVIII of the Constitution?
o: It permits States to secede from the Union during a National Emergency.
It permanently abolishes the federal distribution of powers during every emergency.
It permits the federation to become unitary during specified circumstances without a formal constitutional amendment.
It applies only to Financial Emergency and not to other emergencies.
accepted.x: Part XVIII, comprising Articles 352 to 360, enables the federal system to operate in a unitary manner during emergencies without a formal constitutional amendment.
accepted.tq: Test the scope and constitutional effect of the emergency provisions together.
accepted.sec: Switching between federal and unitary modes - emergency, Art. 249, Art. 356

accepted.s: The statement that the Indian Constitution is “federal in normal times and unitary in emergencies” is associated with:
o: Granville Austin
R. Ambedkar
K. C. Wheare
H. M. Seervai
accepted.x: B. R. Ambedkar characterised the Constitution as federal in normal times and unitary in emergencies.
accepted.tq: Match the constitutional characterisation with its associated thinker.
accepted.sec: Switching between federal and unitary modes - emergency, Art. 249, Art. 356

accepted.s: The distinctive feature that the mode of operation of the Indian Constitution can change from federal to unitary without a constitutional amendment is described as:
o: A conventional feature of all federations
A unique feature of the Indian constitutional system
A feature created by judicial convention after 1994
A feature available only under Article 249
accepted.x: The ability to shift between federal and unitary modes without a formal constitutional amendment is regarded as a unique feature of the Indian constitutional system.
accepted.tq: Identify the exceptional feature rather than confusing it with an ordinary federal characteristic.
accepted.sec: Switching between federal and unitary modes - emergency, Art. 249, Art. 356

accepted.s: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that the Constitution is not truly federal and that the States are not sovereign?
o: State of West Bengal v Union of India
Kesavananda Bharati v State of Kerala
S. R. Bommai v Union of India
Minerva Mills v Union of India
accepted.x: In State of West Bengal v Union of India (1962), the Supreme Court held that the Constitution was not truly federal and that States were not sovereign. The case also concerned Parliament’s power to acquire State property.
accepted.tq: Match the case with its specific judicial characterisation of federalism.
accepted.sec: Supreme Court characterisations of Indian federalism

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the holding in Kesavananda Bharati (1973) concerning federalism?
o: Federal character was recognised as one of the basic features.
States were declared sovereign entities with a right to secede.
Article 356 was held immune from judicial review.
Federalism was excluded from the basic structure.
accepted.x: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) listed the federal character among the basic features of the Constitution.
accepted.tq: Use the basic-structure doctrine as the anchor for identifying the correct holding.
accepted.sec: Supreme Court characterisations of Indian federalism

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding S. R. Bommai v Union of India (1994):
1. Federalism was recognised as part of the basic structure.
2. A proclamation under Article 356 was held open to judicial review.
3. The case placed limits on misuse of Article 356.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements correctly describe the significance of S. R. Bommai v Union of India (1994). The judgment recognised federalism as part of the basic structure and enabled judicial scrutiny of Article 356 proclamations, including through the floor-test principle.
accepted.tq: Link the case to all three related consequences instead of isolating only the basic-structure point.
accepted.sec: Supreme Court characterisations of Indian federalism

accepted.s: Which one of the following formulations best reflects the Supreme Court’s description of Indian federalism in several decisions?
o: Purely federal with no unitary features
Fundamentally federal with pronounced unitary elements
Confederal with sovereign States
Purely unitary with a nominal federal distribution
accepted.x: The Constitution has been described as fundamentally federal with pronounced unitary elements. This reflects the coexistence of federal distribution and strong centralising provisions.
accepted.tq: Choose the precise judicial formulation rather than an extreme description.
accepted.sec: Supreme Court characterisations of Indian federalism

accepted.s:
Assertion (A): Federalism is part of the basic structure of the Indian Constitution.
Reason (R): The Supreme Court recognised the federal character among the basic features in Kesavananda Bharati and reaffirmed federalism’s basic-structure status in S. R. Bommai.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
accepted.x: Both the Assertion and the Reason are true, and the cited constitutional cases directly support the conclusion that federalism forms part of the basic structure.
accepted.tq: Check whether the cited judgments directly establish the constitutional proposition.
accepted.sec: Supreme Court characterisations of Indian federalism
